items.prompt: A UTF-8 CSV starts with field names and contains empty and repeated customer_id values. Which configuration and expected behavior match version 1.0?

options.A: Set header=true, require customer_id, and expect empty or duplicate key rows to be rejected.
options.B: Set header=true and generate replacement IDs for invalid rows.
options.C: Set header=false and make customer_id optional.
options.D: Set header=true and accept duplicate IDs when other columns differ.

items.rationale: A follows I1. B invents ID generation; C misreads headers and required key; D contradicts duplicate rejection.
items.cognitive_level: Apply/analyze documented rules within a scenario
items.intended_challenge: Distinguish adequate evidence from plausible shortcuts; empirical difficulty unknown
items.author: AI draft, fictional Northstar case

items.prompt: Of 1,000 rows, 970 are accepted, 20 rejected for empty keys and 10 for duplicate keys. No exclusion is agreed. What next?

options.A: Publish because accepted plus rejected equals 1,000.
options.B: Retry unchanged input until all rows are accepted.
options.C: Review rejections and document correction or explicitly agreed exclusion before considering publication.
options.D: Publish accepted rows and treat rejected rows as implicitly excluded.

items.rationale: C follows I2. A confuses count agreement with permission; B cannot repair invalid input; D invents agreement.
items.cognitive_level: Apply/analyze documented rules within a scenario
items.intended_challenge: Distinguish adequate evidence from plausible shortcuts; empirical difficulty unknown
items.author: AI draft, fictional Northstar case

items.prompt: A 1,000-row import reports 990 accepted and 5 rejected. What conclusion is supported?

options.A: Treat the five remaining rows as duplicates.
options.B: Investigate the unexplained gap before publication; escalate unresolved discrepancy to the customer data owner.
options.C: Publish because acceptance is at least 99 percent.
options.D: Preview five accepted rows to account for the missing rows.

items.rationale: B follows I2/I3: only 995 rows are accounted for. A invents reasons; C invents threshold; D confuses sampling with accounting.

items.prompt: Counts reconcile and rejection dispositions are documented. A colleague says preview --limit 5 repairs mapping errors and proves readiness. What should you do?

options.A: Use preview to repair, then publish without retaining evidence.
options.B: Treat preview completion as proof that all values are correct.
options.D: Use preview to inspect accepted rows without changing them; check required mappings and representative values, retaining source and reconciliation evidence.

items.rationale: D follows I3. A incorrectly makes preview mutating; B overclaims sampling; C omits verification.

items.prompt: Complete an ingestion evidence sheet and publication recommendation for B-17.
items.setup: Synthetic paper case; no commands executed. Previous published P-16 remains available. UTF-8 CSV header customer_id,amount. Six data rows: 1 C101,10; 2 C102,20; 3 [empty],30; 4 C102,40; 5 C105,50; 6 C106,60. Supplied rejection report: row 3 empty key and row 4 duplicate key. Accepted=4, rejected=2. Configuration: header=true, customer_id required. Preview shows C101/10 and C105/50. Mapping log maps source amount to destination customer_name instead of amount. No exclusion agreed. Treat the report as authoritative about which duplicate row was rejected; do not invent duplicate semantics.
items.deliverable: One sheet with configuration/mapping findings, row accounting, rejection disposition/rerun plan and publication recommendation with evidence and escalation. Distinguish supplied evidence from proposed repairs.

rubric.anchor: 2: identifies appropriate header/key settings AND wrong amount mapping requiring correction; 1: only one; 0: neither or accepts mapping.
2: gives 4+2=6 and says count agreement alone does not authorize release; 1: correct arithmetic without release implication; 0: arithmetic wrong or says totals alone permit release.

2: addresses both invalid keys through correction with owner input or explicit agreed exclusion, then rerun/reconcile; 1: fully handles one or omits agreement/rerun; 0: silent exclusion or unchanged retry as repair.

2: holds pending corrected mapping/dispositions and representative recheck, retains source/reconciliation and previous version, escalates unresolved discrepancy to data owner; 1: holds with incomplete evidence/rechecks/escalation; 0: recommends publication now.

items.rationale: Evidence-sheet exercise integrates documented checks and action planning; it does not observe software execution.

options.B: The service identity reads orders, is denied orders write and is denied unrelated customer datasets.
options.C: The service identity reads orders and has read-only in its name.
options.D: The administrator confirms the account exists.

items.rationale: B follows A2. A tests wrong identity; C omits negative tests; D proves existence only.

items.prompt: A service token was disclosed in a shared note. What follows the documented procedure?

options.A: Revoke the token and obtain authorized replacement; record the incident without the secret.
options.B: Rename the account and keep using the token.
options.C: Create a second token and assume the first stopped working.
options.D: Copy the token into a support ticket for identification.

items.rationale: A follows A3. B/C do not invalidate the old token; D spreads the secret.

items.prompt: Complete an access evidence sheet for svc-orders and a safe remediation sequence.
items.setup: Synthetic paper case; no token supplied or changes executed. Requirement read orders only. Current grant workspace reader. Under svc-orders: orders read succeeds, orders write denied, unrelated customer ledger read succeeds. An administrator read also succeeds. A service token was disclosed in a shared note, represented only as TOKEN_REDACTED.
items.deliverable: One sheet: grant recommendation, interpretation/recheck plan, token response sequence, credential-free incident/evidence record. Mark proposed actions separately from supplied observations.

rubric.anchor: 2: replaces workspace reader with dataset orders reader AND explains unrelated exposure; 1: one only; 0: keeps broad access or grants writer/admin.

2: identifies ledger success as failure and specifies service-identity read success/write denial/unrelated denial after remediation; 1: recognizes exposure but rechecks incomplete; 0: accepts administrator test or existing results as sufficient.
2: revokes disclosed token and gets authorized replacement; 1: only one; 0: rename/add token only or keep using disclosed token.

2: records identity, outcomes and incident/action status without secrets and labels proposed rechecks as proposed; 1: safe record with missing identity/status detail; 0: copies secret or falsely claims remediation happened.

items.rationale: Evidence-sheet exercise integrates documented checks and action planning; it does not observe software execution.

items.prompt: A snapshot is two hours old and no recovery objective is recorded. Where should a rehearsal restore go, and how should age be treated?

options.A: Overwrite active data and assume two hours is acceptable.
options.B: Restore separately and accept any snapshot under one day old.
options.C: Restore into active data after the consultant chooses the objective.
options.D: Restore into a new namespace and escalate the missing customer-approved objective before claiming acceptable loss.

items.rationale: D follows R1. A/C overwrite active data. A/B/C invent authority or acceptable loss windows.

items.prompt: Separate restore counts, representative values and service permissions pass, and age meets the approved objective. What remains before redirecting clients?

options.B: Prepare cutover/rollback recommendation, retain old namespace and obtain customer authorization recording who approved which version.
options.C: Redirect because verification grants incident command authority.
options.D: Redirect now and seek authorization afterward.

items.rationale: B follows R3. A removes rollback; C invents authority; D reverses authorization sequence.

items.prompt: Complete a recovery evidence sheet and recommendation for R-22.
items.setup: Synthetic paper case, no executable lab. Active prod-old remains in service. Immutable S-22 snapshot taken 08:00; decision time 11:00. Customer-approved maximum snapshot age is four hours. Separate restore target rehearsal-new. Manifest count=500; restored=497. Representative IDs/values match supplied manifest examples. Intended service identity reads orders, is denied orders write, but CAN read unrelated customer data. Job status complete. No customer cutover authorization.
items.deliverable: One sheet: age/namespace checks, count/value/permission findings, hold/cutover decision and investigation plan, conditional cutover/rollback and authorization record. Separate observed evidence from required rechecks.

rubric.anchor: 2: computes three-hour age within four-hour objective AND confirms separate namespace protects active data; 1: only one; 0: wrong age or proposes overwrite.
2: identifies three-row mismatch AND excess service access despite completion/sample match; 1: one failure; 0: accepts restore as verified.
2: holds cutover for investigation/correction and repeat counts/values/intended-permission tests; 1: holds with incomplete follow-up; 0: cutover despite a failure.

2: retains prod-old, specifies rollback route to retained namespace and requires customer authorization with actor/exact version before redirect; 1: retains old and requires approval but lacks rollback/version detail; 0: deletes old, redirects unapproved or claims incident command.

items.rationale: Evidence-sheet exercise integrates documented checks and action planning; it does not observe software execution.
